stem: A client has taken alprazolam every day for several months and says, “I feel well, so I’m stopping it today.” Which teaching is most important?

options.A: Stopping today is appropriate because prescribed benzodiazepine use does not produce clinically important physical dependence.
options.B: Take a double dose every other day for one week and then stop because intermittent high doses prevent withdrawal more safely than a taper.
options.C: Do not stop abruptly; continued benzodiazepine use can cause physical dependence, and dose reduction should follow a gradual patient-specific taper.
options.D: Continue the current dose indefinitely because any attempt to taper a benzodiazepine is more dangerous than remaining on long-term therapy.

rationale: Current alprazolam labeling warns that continued benzodiazepine use can cause physical dependence and that abrupt discontinuation or rapid dosage reduction can precipitate acute, potentially life-threatening withdrawal. A gradual taper is therefore required. C is correct; A denies dependence, B invents an unsafe regimen, and D incorrectly treats tapering as contraindicated.
educational_objective: Teach clients not to abruptly stop chronic benzodiazepine therapy and to follow an individualized gradual taper.
source_locator: Boxed Warning; §2.3 Discontinuation or Dosage Reduction; §5.3 Dependence and Withdrawal Reactions.
source_claim_supported: Continued alprazolam use can cause physical dependence; abrupt cessation/rapid reduction can cause severe withdrawal and requires gradual tapering.

source_original.rationale: Current alprazolam labeling warns that continued benzodiazepine use can produce physical dependence and that abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction can precipitate acute, potentially life-threatening withdrawal.
